messages.subject: stat_boxplot code question
parts:
Hello list,

Perhaps I am not being resourceful enough, and if that's true,
I apologize in advance.

I draw a simple boxplot in ggplot, and want to know what percentile
of the data the whiskers extend to (assuming that's how it is
defined?).

I'm guessing I want the code to the stat_boxplot function, but
that simply returns:

function (mapping = NULL, data = NULL, geom = "boxplot", position =
"dodge",
na.rm = FALSE, coef = 1.5, ...)
StatBoxplot$new(mapping = mapping, data = data, geom = geom,
position = position, na.rm = na.rm, coef = coef, ...)

Since I am familiar with the proto package (which I think this
is using), I do not know how to see the code. Can anyone help?

Thanks,
--Erik

messages.author: 1c4479e879526ead
messages.subject: Re: stat_boxplot code question
parts:
Two small amendments:
I am *un*familiar with proto, and I do realize that I am
seeing the code of the stat_boxplot function when I print
its value. What I want to know is how to see the code that
implements the finding of the box and whiskers values, which
I assume has something to do with StatBoxplot, but I am
not sure how to proceed.

Best,
--Erik

does refer you to the webpage

your question.

Best,

messages.subject: Re: stat_boxplot code question
parts:
Hi,

It seems the following proto idioms can take you some way,

## List the content of the proto object
StatBoxplot$ls()

## See the code for the calculation
StatBoxplot$calculate

etc.

HTH,

baptiste
